methodological_rigor.justification: This is a descriptive case series integrating nuclear morphometry (~317 nuclei per sample traced manually by a single blinded investigator), IHC (brachyury, Ki-67, p53, lamin A/C, SMARCB1, VEGF, EGFR, S100, PD-1/PD-L1, E-cadherin), and whole-exome sequencing in 26 specimens from only 12 patients (8 non-recurrent, 4 long-term recurrent). Strengths: specimen-level medians as primary unit, Bland-Altman duplicate analysis (bias 0.14 um2), WES with clear variant filters (MAF<0.001, VAF>=0.1, read-index>=40), Friedman tests with Bonferroni adjustment for longitudinal comparisons, Mann-Whitney U for between-group tests. However, the 4-patient recurrent group, unequal longitudinal timepoints, and multiple comparisons across morphometric parameters without global FDR control severely limit inference. The authors explicitly acknowledge that longitudinal p-values are exploratory. Manual tracing by one investigator introduces subjectivity despite blinding, and pre-analytical variability across archival samples spanning different time periods confounds pixel-based density measures.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Descriptive case series with 12 patients maps to Oxford LoE 4. The translational goal (developing morphometry-based AI tools for chordoma recurrence risk stratification) is clinically interesting given the paucity of prognostic markers in this rare tumor, but the evidence is preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Authors appropriately frame findings as requiring validation in larger cohorts and do not claim clinical utility.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods are detailed for sample selection (n=26 from 12 patients, archival Bone Tumor Registry), IHC protocols (automated Ventana NexES, antibody clones, dilutions), morphometry (NIS Elements D v4.20.03, systematic field selection, >=300 nuclei per sample), and WES pipeline (SureSelect XT HS2, NextSeq 550, Varvis v1.21.2, GRCh37 alignment, filter thresholds). Ethics approval is reported (132/21). However, STROBE items are incomplete: no explicit sample size justification, no flow diagram, limited handling of missing data discussion, and multiple comparison correction is applied only per-case via Bonferroni without cohort-wide FDR. No data or code availability statement; WES raw data deposition not indicated.

novelty_literature.justification: The study is positioned as the first to integrate longitudinal quantitative nuclear morphometry with WES-derived TMB and IHC in long-term recurrent/metastatic chordoma, which is a meaningful niche contribution given chordoma rarity. Nuclear morphometry in recurrence contexts has been reported in other tumors (soft tissue sarcoma, osteosarcoma, DCIS, Wilms tumor), so the methodology is established but novel in application to chordoma. The lamin A/C disintegration observation in pleomorphic nuclei offers a plausible mechanistic link but is qualitative.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is logically structured and reasonably well written, with clear IMRaD organization, detailed methods, and interpretive Discussion. Figures and tables are referenced and mapping between morphometric parameters and biological interpretation is explained. Limitations section explicitly covers three main issues (archival preanalytical variability, small sample size, clinical heterogeneity). Weaknesses include repetitive content in the Discussion (e.g., patient 10 paragraph duplicated verbatim) and occasional awkward phrasings; one REDACTED blinding artifact in Section 3.1.

key_strengths: Novel longitudinal integration of nuclear morphometry, IHC, and WES in long-term recurrent/metastatic chordoma (7-16 year follow-up)
Duplicate-section reproducibility check with Bland-Altman bias of 0.14 um2
Blinded single-rater morphometry with ~317 nuclei per sample and systematic field selection
Biologically coherent finding of lamin A/C loss correlating with nuclear pleomorphism across recurrences
Transparent framing as descriptive and hypothesis-generating with explicit validation requirement
key_concerns: Only 12 patients (4 recurrent), with unequal numbers of longitudinal timepoints, yielding severely underpowered longitudinal and group comparisons
Multiple comparison correction applied per-case only; no cohort-wide FDR across morphometric parameters
Archival FFPE samples spanning different time periods may confound pixel-based density measures; no pre-analytical standardization possible
No data/code availability statement; WES raw data deposition not indicated
Manual nuclear tracing by single investigator limits reproducibility; no AI validation despite framing as precursor to AI applications
Duplicated content in Discussion (patient 10 paragraph verbatim twice)
chief_reviewer.rationale: Small descriptive chordoma case series integrating morphometry, IHC, and WES with transparent limitations; substantial underpowering and pre-analytical variability limit inference, placing this at Tier 4 with major revisions to strengthen reporting and validation framing.
